sentences.text:
Heard Sri.Shantharaj.K, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.B.Pradeep, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

Being aggrieved by the sum that is awarded as compensation by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hassan through orders in MVC No.1082/2018 dated 13.07.2022, the claimant therein filed the present appeal seeking enhancement in compensation.
3. Arguing the matter, learned counsel for the appellant states that appellant sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred in 2016.
As per the evidence of Cw.1, she suffers with functional disability of 28.93% in respect of right lower limb.
But the Tribunal did not award any compensation towards loss of future earnings.
Learned counsel also states that compensation granted under all heads is also on lower side.
NC: 2026:KHC:6476 HC-KAR 4.
Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the appellant got examined herself as Pw.1.
During the course of cross-examination, she clearly admitted that she is drawing salary of Rs.55,000/- per month.
That itself shows that there is no loss of future earnings due to alleged disability.
Learned counsel further states that in the light of submission that is made by learned counsel for the appellant there may be marginal enhancement.

5. Through all the evidence produced, appellant succeeded in establishing that she sustained an abrasion over right gluteal region, lacerated wounds on left cheek, over left forearm, on right leg and over anterolateral aspect of left knee.
That she sustained nasal bone fracture, fracture shaft of right tibia and incomplete fracture of medial tibial spine.
The version of the appellant is that she was working as Second Division Assistant and Typist.

As rightly contented by learned counsel for respondent No.2 which is not disputed by learned counsel NC: 2026:KHC:6476 HC-KAR for appellant, appellant continues her job and gets a salary of Rs.55,000/- per month.
However as per the evidence of Cw.1 appellant suffers with disability of 28.93% in respect of right lower limb.
Therefore, appellant has to attend her duties as well as day to day routine activities with such disability.

The Tribunal granted a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.67,444/-
towards medical expenses, Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities, Rs.25,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period and Rs.10,000/- towards food, nourishment and other miscellaneous expenses.
Thus the Tribunal granted a sum of Rs.1,78,000/- in total as compensation.

However considering the nature of injuries sustained, extensive treatment taken and the disability with which the appellant is left with, this Court is of the view that compensation granted under all heads except medical expenses is on lower side.

Though the appellant in stricto sensu is not entitled for any compensation towards loss of future earnings however, appellant will have to incur more NC:
2026:KHC:6476 HC-KAR expenditure than others for all purposes including travelling to office.
Therefore, considering all these aspects this Court is of the view that the compensation granted by the Tribunal is required to be enhanced.

This Court is also of the view that in case additional sum of Kalavathi C K vs Rangappa on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47811121/
3 Rs.1,25,000/- is granted, the total sum which the appellant receives will be justifiable.

Therefore,
the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hassan through orders in MVC No.1082/2018 dated 13.07.2022 is enhanced by Rs.1,25,000/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of 8(eight) NC: 2026:KHC:6476 HC-KAR weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(v) On such deposit, appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.

Sd/-
(DR.CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) JUDGE NS CT:TSM List No.: 1 Sl No.: 27 Kalavathi C K vs Rangappa on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47811121/
